controls_available.scope: The three visible brass handles on the NORTH, SOUTHWEST, and SOUTHEAST discs
controls_available.effect: A drag of at least 0.45 radians requests one clockwise or counter-clockwise sixth-turn; the sign of the drag selects the direction.
Administrative submission after the rose has been restored; it does not change the rose during the solve.
Requests a fresh challenge and is not part of a successful normal solve.

autonomous_processes.period: Between all agent inputs, including live idle time
autonomous_processes.reason: The rose model has no task timer, interval, animation loop, physics loop, or autonomous state update. A visible rose change occurs only when an input handler attempts a turn.

grouped_control_modes.scope: Every outcome-affecting drag attempt on any of the three handles, in either direction, across seeds and turns
grouped_control_modes.effect: A legal request rotates the selected disc; an illegal request is synchronously refused and leaves the state unchanged.

clause_i.reason: An observation-free q cannot choose the shortest-path progress action for every occurrence of rim_drag: the generator selects different depth-seven initial states by seed, while I_t does not contain the visible rose. The same empty action history can therefore require different disc/direction choices.

clause_ii.reason: For the state-choice portion, a zero-width bounded window is sufficient: the screenshot shows the current stained-glass arrangement and the reference arrangement, and the fixed disc geometry and turn rules allow a visual policy g to select a shortest-path disc and direction. This is static visual grounding, not evidence of a changing process.

clause_iii.reason: No positive Delta can witness autonomous degradation. With no new action, the current state remains unchanged, so an action's Q value and advantage over no-op do not strictly decrease. Legal-turn eligibility changes only synchronously after attempt() receives a drag; clock progression, later completion, or a deadline cannot satisfy the non-clock task-state requirement.

common_visible_process: None. The only outcome-affecting visual change is the synchronous result of a drag; CSS hover/drag styling and shared clock progression do not change the rose task state.

pre_run.reason: The source has no autonomous outcome phase. Every successful restoration requires outcome-affecting turns delivered by the agent, while SEAL is administrative; therefore no generated instance admits the specified action-free pre-run form.

source_evidence.claim: The frozen definition requires a common visible autonomous process and a strict loss in action value or advantage caused by non-clock task-state evolution.
Difficulty 3 is medium and sets scramble_depth to 7.
Full interaction is rim_drag, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame; play time is 180 seconds.
Disc legality and turns are deterministic state transformations; generation samples a seed-dependent state at the selected BFS depth and records a solved state and exact optimal distance.
The browser implements synchronous legality/turn logic, and current state changes only inside attempt(), which is invoked by an input. Refused turns leave the state unchanged.
Full mode renders drag handles, triggers one turn only on a completed drag exceeding the angular threshold, initializes from initial_state, and binds SEAL separately for submission.
The mechanic CSS contains static layout, hover/drag styling, and synchronous pass/fail display rules, with no autonomous animation declaration.
The grader binds full mode to rim_drag and grades by deterministic replay of the submitted turn transcript and final solved state, with no timing condition.
The exported verifier independently replays the same state transitions and decides pass solely from the resulting solved state.
The solver delivers each solution move as an explicit mouse drag in full mode and waits for the successful-turn count after each move; there is no action-free outcome phase.

The shared clock can drain registered timers or run observation windows, but this mechanic registers no timer, frame callback, or clock-dependent state update, so clock progression alone does not evolve the rose.
The verifier's shared helper only copies and parses the exported result; it adds no task-state or timing behavior.
